text:
sarah.m: Hey team, getting a customer escalation — frequent 502/504s hitting the hosted API (edge). Customer sees it when sending bursty h2 requests with auth header + billing-id. Started ~09:10 UTC, 20% failure rate.

raj.k: Can you paste the failure pattern from their curl or stack?

sarah.m: They shared curl and trace ids. Curl looks normal but we see upstream reset and envoy 502s. Example from customer: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Billing-Account: acct-9c3" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

mike_ops: I pulled traces for trace ids they gave. Envoy logs show: `upstream connection error or reset` and `503/504` in some cases. There are repeated `recv() failed` and `RST_STREAM`.

emily_repro: I spun up a repro client that replays their pattern (10 concurrent h2 streams, keepalive enabled, many short requests). Repro is consistent: ~15-25% 502s when throughput spikes.

raj.k: Sounds like h2 connection pool exhaustion / stream resets. Any upstream logs from the inference pods?

mike_ops: Backend logs show authentication lookup latency spikes (~250-500ms) for certain tokens (billing lookup path). When auth backend is slow, the upstream holds the h2 stream open, total concurrency hits limit and Envoy resets. See snippet:

```
2026-03-14T09:12:18Z service-auth lookup billing acct-9c3 latency=420ms
2026-03-14T09:12:18Z inference-handler accept stream id=3145 processing_ms=12
2026-03-14T09:12:18Z proxy upstream write error: connection reset by peer
```

sarah.m: Customer says errors are mostly on models with long init (large context) but also on short requests when they burst.

john.p: Hypothesis: auth/billing lookup is synchronous per request and stalls response write; Envoy h2 max concurrent streams per connection default (100?) gets hit, plus our upstream idle/read/write timeouts cause connection resets => 502.

raj.k: Do we have evidence of h2 stream limit being reached on the frontdoor? Envoy stats?

mike_ops: Envoy metrics show `downstream_rq_active_h2_streams` occasionally spiking to configured max for that node pool. Also `upstream_cx_idle_timeout` fired for several connections around error windows.

emily_repro: Repro commands I used:

```
# simple repro client (golang http2) - 10 concurrent goroutines, 50 reqs each
go run repro.go --concurrency 10 --requests 50 --h2
```

and I toggled auth-cache off/on. With auth-cache enabled, failure rate drops to ~2%.

sarah.m: Customer currently on hosted API, not dedicated. They're asking for timeline and mitigation; they are losing production traffic.

raj.k: Short-term mitigations: 1) Turn on conservative retries at edge for upstream 502 with idempotent requests (client layer) 2) Enable short TTL prefix caching for auth/billing results to avoid synchronous lookups 3) Increase h2 concurrent streams / connection pool size for frontdoor nodes serving this region 4) Add circuit-breaker on auth lookup to fail fast.

mike_ops: Also add per-route upstream drain/backpressure to avoid single tenant hogging streams. We can rate-limit by billing account at edge if they opt-in.

john.p: We should also inspect if token rotation from the customer's side causes repeated cold lookup that thundering herds the auth DB. Ask them for token churn rate.

sarah.m: Customer responded: they rotate tokens every 20s in their client pool. They said token rotation is part of their security flow.

raj.k: That's high. Recommend they extend token TTL or enable a client-side token cache. As a platform side we can add an intermediate token cache layer in front of auth service to absorb churn.

emily_repro: Actionable repro notes I added to the ticket: steps to reproduce, repro client, env vars, and a toggle to enable auth-cache which mitigates.

mike_ops: Short-term rollout plan: deploy config to enable auth result LRU cache in auth service (ttl 30s), bump envoy h2 stream limit from 100 -> 200 on a small canary fleet, and enable 1 retry for upstream 502 with jittered backoff. Also add alerting for `downstream_rq_active_h2_streams > 0.9*limit` per node.

raj.k: Risk of increasing h2 streams: can amplify memory usage. We'll canary on two nodes with load testing. If memory jump <10% and error rate improves, roll.

sarah.m: Customer asked for explanation. Drafted message: "We're seeing the auth/billing lookup occasionally slow under high token churn which causes upstream to hold streams and hit h2 concurrency limits at the edge, resulting in Envoy returning 502/504. We're rolling a short-term cache and connection tuning while we build a more robust token cache and apply rate-limiting per billing account." Thoughts?

john.p: Sounds good. Add suggested customer actions: increase token TTL, enable client-side caching, and add exponential backoff on 5xx before retrying.

deploybot: Deploy queued: canary-auth-cache-v1 -> 2 nodes, canary-envoy-config-h2limit -> 2 nodes. CI checks passed.

mike_ops: I'm kicking the canary now. Will monitor traces and envoy metrics.

sarah.m: I'll update the customer and ask for temporary token TTL change.

raj.k: Postmortem notes to collect: window of errors, affected customer tokens, envoy node ids, upstream pod ids, auth lookup timings, and whether billing header triggered downstream path.

emily_repro: I'll add the repro artifacts and the exact curl/trace ids to the support ticket.

sarah.m: Thanks all — will follow up once canary shows green or we see further anomalies. :thumbsup:

mike_ops: Canary looks promising so far, 502s down from 18% -> 1.8% on canary nodes after auth-cache. Still watching autoscaling metrics.

sarah.m: Sending customer update now.

john.p: Follow-up: schedule a whiteboard session to design a long-term token cache + auth async path to avoid blocking inference request threads.

sarah.m: Noted. Closing thread for now, will reopen if errors resurge.
